profile.name: Maria Rodriguez
profile.bio: Maria Rodriguez is the Republican nominee for Kentucky's 3rd congressional district and works as a cleaning contractor. Her campaign describes a path from political persecution abroad to public service in the United States.

platform.point: Lists safer streets in Louisville as a top priority.
Promotes lower taxes and defending capitalism and free enterprise.
Emphasizes legal immigration as a campaign priority.
Lists protecting the unborn among her priorities.
Pledges to protect women's sports.

economy.evidence: Campaign lists lower taxes and defending capitalism as priorities.

liberty.evidence: Campaign priorities include protecting the unborn (abortion) and protecting women's sports (LGBTQ issues).

profile.name: Ned Pillersdorf
profile.bio: Ned Pillersdorf is an eastern Kentucky attorney who has practiced law for over four decades, much of it representing low-income clients and people with disability claims. He was a candidate for this district in 1992 and is the Democratic nominee in 2026.

platform.point: Opposes cuts to Medicaid, Medicare, food stamps, utility assistance and job training.
Wants to expand health care access and protect rural hospitals affected by Medicaid cuts.
Opposes further tax breaks for the wealthiest Americans.
Prioritizes rural broadband and safe drinking water in eastern Kentucky.
Pledges to defend Social Security, including service staffing.

economy.evidence: Criticizes tax breaks for billionaires and opposes the 2025 budget law.

welfare.evidence: Opposes cuts to Medicaid, Medicare, food stamps and utility assistance and wants expanded health access.

profile.notes: No dedicated issues page was found; the campaign image on the site appears to be a logo rather than a headshot.

profile.name: Ralph Alvarado
profile.bio: Ralph Alvarado is a physician who served in the Kentucky State Senate from 2015 to 2023, the first Hispanic member of the Kentucky General Assembly, and was Tennessee's health commissioner from 2023 to 2025. He was Matt Bevin's running mate for lieutenant governor in 2019. Born in California, he trained at Loma Linda University and the University of Kentucky and practices in Central Kentucky.

platform.point: Wants more affordable care, clearer insurance choices and more patient control.
Focuses on lowering prices for groceries, gas and health care.
Aims to grow jobs in Kentucky.
Pledges to eliminate wasteful government spending.

economy.evidence: Sponsored medical malpractice tort reform as a state senator and campaigns on cutting wasteful spending.

profile.name: Caleb Walker
profile.current_role: Student body president, South Louisiana Community College
profile.bio: Caleb Walker served 10 years in the U.S. Army, reaching Sergeant First Class and deploying to Afghanistan. Originally from Wisner in Franklin Parish, he moved to Lafayette in 2020 and worked as a Sam's Club department manager and community coordinator. He studies political science at South Louisiana Community College, where he is student body president, and serves on the Louisiana Task Force for Career Alignment.

profile.name: Conrad Cable
profile.bio: Conrad Cable is a farmer from Farmerville in north Louisiana. He is running as a Democrat for the 4th District, campaigning on agriculture, health care and worker issues.

platform.point: Supports Medicare for All and opposes federal cuts to Medicaid.
Wants higher wages and stronger protections for union organizing.
Proposes public grocery stores in rural and low-income areas stocked with local food and accepting SNAP and WIC.
Backs overturning Citizens United and banning stock trading by members of Congress.
Argues current farm and trade policy has hurt Louisiana soybean growers.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and opposes Medicaid cuts.
